rounds.text: Linc Ltd is materially under-appreciated by the market, trading at a modest P/E of 16.9x [E1] and sitting only 32% of the way up its 52-week range despite robust underlying operational efficiency [E5]. The company demonstrates exceptional asset productivity, delivering a return on assets (ROA) of 9.77% which dwarfs the sector benchmark of 3.52% [E8]. Medium-term growth has been explosive, highlighted by a compounded profit growth of 250% over the last 5 years [E19]. Furthermore, future growth catalysts are already heavily funded, with Capital Work in Progress (CWIP) surging by 126.7% to reach Rs 34 Cr by March 2026, signaling an aggressive and active capex build-up phase [E41]. Recent operational momentum is also confirmed by accelerating earnings growth, sales being up quarter-on-quarter, and a multi-year sales uptrend [E64, E65, E66]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months stands at -5% [E21] and over the last 3 years is -1% [E20].

The recent financial trajectory reveals a clear deceleration, marked by a 1% decline in compounded profit growth over 3 years and a further 5% drop over the trailing twelve months [E20, E21]. This earnings contraction is compounded by a 9% year-on-year drop in sales flagged by the screen [E68]. Furthermore, the hefty capital expenditure phase signalled by a 126.7% surge in capital work-in-progress to ₹ 34 Cr by March 2026 introduces execution and capital allocation risks [E41]. Meanwhile, the price-to-book ratio of 2.26x trades at a premium to the sector benchmark of 1.83x, suggesting the valuation leaves little room for error given the stalling growth [E7]. Conceded: the company boasts a 5-year compounded profit growth of 250% and an ROA of 9.77% that outperforms the sector benchmark of 3.52% [E8, E19].

The bear's focus on recent stagnation ignores the extraordinary 250% compounded profit growth achieved over five years, which dwarfs any short-term deceleration [E19]. While three-year and trailing twelve-month growth dipped slightly by -1% and -5% respectively, the screen explicitly catches earnings growth accelerating alongside a multi-year sales uptrend and QoQ sales increases [E20, E21, E64, E65, E66]. The 126.7% surge in capital work-in-progress to ₹ 34 Cr by March 2026 is not a risk but a deliberate, active growth spend underway as expansion phase infrastructure comes online [E41]. Conceded: sales dropped 9% year-on-year [E68]. However, this cyclical top-line softness is offset by an exceptional Return on Assets of 9.77% that nearly triples the sector benchmark of 3.52%, proving superior operational efficiency even in a transitional period [E8]. Finally, the P/E ratio of 16.9x to 18.26x is entirely reasonable and aligns closely with the broader sector benchmark of 18.84x, meaning the market is not over-pricing the equity given these asset-level strengths [E1, E6].

Conceded: five-year compounded profit growth reached 250% [E19]. However, that historic surge is completely detached from the company's current reality, where three-year compounded profit growth has stalled at -1% and trailing twelve-month growth has worsened to -5% [E20, E21]. The bull downplays a verified 9% year-on-year drop in sales as mere cyclical softness, ignoring that this top-line contraction directly contradicts any notion of ongoing momentum [E68]. Furthermore, the massive 126.7% spike in Capital Work-In-Progress to ₹ 34 Cr by March 2026 represents a heavy capital commitment during a period of declining trailing earnings, creating a significant execution and return risk rather than an unmitigated positive [E41]. Finally, while the Price-to-Book ratio of 2.26x to 2.37x may look modest, it already commands a clear premium over the sector benchmark of 1.83x, leaving very little margin of safety for a business experiencing negative near-term profit and sales growth [E2, E7, E21, E68].
